## Implementation — `collect_partitioned` in `fetch_paging.py`

`_ACLI_CEILING` stays at **1200** and `_iter_pages` is **byte-unchanged**. The fix is a new
drain that runs *around* the pager, not through it.

### Shape

`drain(client, jql, page_size, cap)` routes one base query by its shape:

- **`cap is None`** — the exhaustive active query. Goes to `collect_partitioned`.
- **`cap is not None`** — the `ORDER BY updated DESC` done-recent query. Stays on the
  single-query path. Partitioning a top-N read would silently change *which* issues it
  selects, so `collect_partitioned` **refuses an `ORDER BY` query with a `ValueError`**
  rather than mis-slicing it. (It also cannot reach the ceiling: the cap returns at 1,000.)

`collect_partitioned` begins as the **single unbounded query** — byte-identical to what runs
today — and only subdivides a window that *actually* raises the ceiling. A project under the
ceiling issues exactly the one query it always did; nothing changes until it has to.

On `SilentTruncationError(reason="ceiling")` it replaces window `[lo, hi)` with `[lo, mid)`
and `[mid, hi)` and re-asks. Windows are drained left to right off a LIFO, so the union comes
back in `created` order.

### Why it cannot silently drop a slice

1. **The split is structurally exhaustive.** `[lo, mid) + [mid, hi)` covers exactly `[lo, hi)`
   with no gap and no overlap **for any `mid`**. Coverage does not depend on choosing `mid`
   well — only the probe count does. There is no arithmetic that can be off by one, because
   the same `mid` value is the upper bound of one window and the lower bound of the next.
2. **No sentinel dates.** The leftmost window omits `created >=` entirely and the rightmost
   omits `created <`, so the outer edges stay genuinely unbounded. Nothing assumes a project
   start date, and issues created *while the pass runs* still fall in the last window.
3. **The partition key is immutable.** `created` never changes, so no issue migrates across a
   boundary mid-pass. `updated` would have exactly that flaw.
4. **The boundary need not exist.** This is what killed `issuekey` (see the measurement
   comment): `created < X` and `created >= X` are complementary for any instant X.
5. **Only the ceiling is ever intercepted.** `same-token-twice` and `offset-stall` propagate
   out of any slice and abort the whole fetch — they are not retried as bisections, because a
   stalled slice is untrustworthy, not merely too big.
6. **The guard is preserved, not weakened.** When a window is already at Jira's finest
   expressible resolution (one minute) the ceiling is **re-raised**. This path never returns a
   partial slice; it only replaces one over-large *complete* read with several smaller
   *complete* reads.

### A new defence the tests forced out: the window-blind server

Running the existing suite surfaced a real hole. A client that **ignores the `created`
predicate** (returns the full set for every window) can never be narrowed into compliance, so
the walk-back doubled its span until Python's date arithmetic threw `OverflowError` — an
unhandled crash, and ~16 futile full drains first. This is the window-level sibling of the
existing offset-stall check (server ignoring `startAt`).

Fixed with `_MAX_SPAN` (40 years): past any plausible project history, the drain stops and
re-raises the **ceiling**, loudly, after 11 probes instead of 16-plus-a-crash. That also fixed
a pre-existing test (`test_fetch_at_1200_issue_ceiling_raises_silent_truncation_error`) whose
stub is exactly such a client.

### Mutation results — 10/10 killed

Each mutation was applied to `fetch_paging.py` in isolation and reverted after:

| Mutation | Verdict |
|---|---|
| drop the right slice | CAUGHT |
| drop the left slice | CAUGHT |
| gap at the seam (right child starts one minute late) | CAUGHT |
| overlapping union (left child keeps the full upper bound) | CAUGHT |
| half-open window becomes closed (`created <=`) | CAUGHT |
| lower bound becomes exclusive (`created >`) | CAUGHT |
| swallow every truncation reason, not just the ceiling | CAUGHT |
| return a partial when the window cannot be split | CAUGHT |
| drop the window-blind (`_MAX_SPAN`) guard | CAUGHT |
| route the capped top-N query through the partitioner too | CAUGHT |

Two of these **survived the first round** and drove real test work rather than being written
up as passes:

- *gap at the seam* survived because the fixture's 17-minute issue spacing meant a one-minute
  hole rarely landed on an issue. Closed two ways: a **structural** assertion that the
  windows which actually completed chain end-to-end (first unbounded below, last unbounded
  above, every `hi` equal to the next `lo`) — which catches a gap regardless of data density —
  and a dense fixture at one issue per minute so every seam lands on a populated minute.
- *drop the `_MAX_SPAN` guard* survived because the `OverflowError` fallback still produced
  the right verdict, just slowly. Closed by asserting the probe budget (measured: 11 with the
  guard, 16 without).

The `swallow every truncation reason` mutant is worth calling out: it makes
`test_offset_stall_in_a_later_slice_still_raises` report **DID NOT RAISE** — i.e. that mutant
returns a silent partial snapshot. That is this bug's exact failure mode, and the seam tests
catch it.

### Cost

Against the measured REB shape (1,388 active) the drain settles at roughly six windows, four
of which are ceiling probes — about 100 ACLI calls where today's (failing) query makes 14.
The pass already runs ~20 minutes dominated by enrichment, so this is not material, and the
probe count is logarithmic rather than proportional to project size. Noting it rather than
hiding it.

### Files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py` — `collect_partitioned`, `drain`,
  `_window_jql`, `_split_window` (190 -> 391 lines; cap is 800).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — `_fetch_project` calls `drain`. The
  routing policy moved into `fetch_paging` specifically so this file stays at **650** lines,
  the explicit target `test_fetch_paging_split.py` asserts (it went to 667 first).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_partitioned_fetch.py` — 17 tests.

### AC status

- **AC1** measured and recorded — growth, widening refuted (previous comment).
- **AC2** `rebar bridge run` against live REB — **NOT verified by me.** Running the reconciler
  live is a bridge *write* against a third-party system and is the operator's call. Verified
  by proxy at the measured working-set size in `test_fetch_project_drains_the_measured_working_set_completely`.
- **AC3** `_ACLI_CEILING` unchanged at 1200, with a regression test asserting it.
- **AC4** demonstrated at 1,388 / 3,000 / 5,000 issues against a 1,200 ceiling.
- **AC5** all three defences proven in a LATER slice, plus the new window-blind defence.
- **AC6** workflow returns to green — pending merge; not verifiable pre-landing.
